region: Burdett · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Ryan William Vineyard is a family-run farm winery in Burdett, on the east shore of Seneca Lake, owned and founded by Ryan Bossert. Vineyard, cellar, tasting room and the Tasting Barn restaurant share one hillside above the lake, and Bossert describes the aim simply: to let the grapes express the character of the vineyard. That approach was rewarded in August 2026, when the winery took the Governor’s Cup, the top prize of the New York Wine Classic, for its 2025 Pinot Blanc.

Riesling is the grape that made the Finger Lakes’ reputation, and Seneca Lake’s east shore is one of its best addresses: the lake’s deep water moderates the climate, letting the grapes hang into autumn while keeping their acidity. This wine carries the Seneca Lake appellation, meaning the fruit comes from the slopes around the lake, and it is made in a dry style. Expect peach and slate on the nose, light pineapple on the palate and a lively, lime-edged finish.
